allObjections.title: Credential fallback creates security debt
allObjections.detail: §3.2's PAT fallback path contradicts the security posture by maintaining long-lived tokens in Doppler even after claiming 'memory-only' in §3.3. The INTERIM label doesn't eliminate the attack surface during Phase A's entire lifetime.

allObjections.title: Re-assessment cost doubles operator burden
allObjections.detail: §6.2 requires running the full 8-step pipeline twice per renewal, costing $0.65-$5.00 per run (Note 3). For products under continuous crawl (Locked Rule 14), this could mean hundreds of dollars monthly with no guarantee of positive outcomes.

allObjections.title: Preview-smoke gate has trivial bypass
allObjections.detail: §4.4 gate (c) accepts default selectors ['html', 'body'] which any broken app satisfies. A completely white-screened React app with a JS error still passes because the HTML skeleton renders, making this gate theatrical rather than functional.

allObjections.title: Delta score computation ignores user experience
allObjections.detail: §6.3 computes delta purely from Five-Layer Framework scores, but a fix that improves L2 Operational metrics while breaking critical user flows would show positive delta. No gate validates actual user-facing functionality preservation.

allObjections.title: Credential management complexity
allObjections.detail: Section §3.2 introduces a dual credential model with GitHub App as primary and PAT as an interim fallback. This increases complexity and potential security risks, as managing two credential paths can lead to misconfigurations or overlooked security vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: Limited regression detection
allObjections.detail: Section §2 acknowledges that Self-Renewal cannot guarantee fixes won't introduce regressions, relying solely on human review. This could lead to undetected issues in production if human reviewers miss subtle regressions.

allObjections.title: High operational cost
allObjections.detail: Section §6.2 and Note 3 highlight the cost of running the full 8-step pipeline twice per renewal, potentially reaching $5.00 per run. This could become financially unsustainable for operators with frequent renewals or multiple products.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient testing for the Self-Renewal feature, which could lead to unforeseen consequences and errors. Specifically, §4.4 only mentions testing for syntax and type errors, but does not account for other potential issues such as performance or security vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: Over-Reliance on Claude
allObjections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on Claude for fix generation, which may not always produce optimal or correct results. This could lead to a situation where the Self-Renewal feature introduces more problems than it solves. §4.1 mentions that Claude is used for fix generation, but does not provide any information on how its performance will be evaluated or improved.

allObjections.title: Lack of Human Oversight
allObjections.detail: While the proposal mentions that human review is required for PRs, it does not provide sufficient details on how this oversight will be implemented or enforced. This could lead to a situation where the Self-Renewal feature is used without proper human review, potentially introducing errors or security vulnerabilities. §5.3 mentions that the PR is created in draft state, but does not specify how the human review process will be conducted.

allObjections.title: Over-reliance on Claude
allObjections.detail: The proposal heavily relies on Claude for fix generation. This introduces a significant risk as Claude's outputs can be unpredictable and may not always adhere to the expected standards. This reliance could lead to inconsistent or incorrect fixes, which could compromise the integrity of the codebase.

allObjections.title: Complexity of Discard Gates
allObjections.detail: The fix-discard gates in §4.4 introduce multiple layers of complexity. The gates are crucial for ensuring the quality of the fixes, but the implementation details are intricate and could be prone to errors. The proposal does not provide a clear mechanism for handling edge cases where a fix might pass some gates but fail others.

allObjections.title: Security Risks with PAT
allObjections.detail: The use of fine-grained PATs, even as an interim fallback, poses security risks. PATs are less secure compared to GitHub Apps, and their usage could lead to unauthorized access or misuse. The proposal should emphasize the security benefits of using GitHub Apps and provide a clearer pathway for transitioning away from PATs.

allObjections.title: Credential Management
allObjections.detail: The proposal relies on a fine-grained PAT as an interim fallback, which could pose security risks if not managed properly. The fallback should be removed as soon as possible to avoid potential vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: Limited Scope
allObjections.detail: The current scope of the proposal is limited to single-file fixes, which may not be sufficient for more complex issues that require multi-file changes.

allObjections.title: Human Dependency
allObjections.detail: The proposal heavily relies on human review for merging PRs and catching regressions, which could introduce delays and inconsistencies in the renewal process.

allObjections.title: Credential Fallback Complexity
allObjections.detail: §3.2 introduces significant complexity with the GitHub App primary and PAT fallback.  Managing two credential paths increases the attack surface and operational overhead, especially during the transition period. The logic for selecting and validating the correct credential adds potential for errors and vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: Limited Regression Detection
allObjections.detail: §2 acknowledges the inability to guarantee no regressions, relying heavily on human review.  While §7.5 mentions Phase D will address this, the current reliance on human review is a significant risk, especially as the number of automated fixes increases. The test suite may not cover all edge cases, and visual regressions can easily be missed.

allObjections.title: Re-assessment Cost
allObjections.detail: §6.2 and Note 3 highlight the cost of re-running the full 8-step pipeline for re-assessment.  This doubles the assessment cost and significantly increases the overall cost of the Self-Renewal cycle.  The cost may become prohibitive, especially for products with frequent renewal runs.

allObjections.title: Preview Smoke Test Weakness
allObjections.detail: §4.4 (c) defines the preview smoke test as checking for HTTP 2xx and at least one key DOM element. The default DOM element check of `['html', 'body']` is effectively useless.  Even with stricter selectors, this provides minimal assurance that the preview is actually functional or visually correct.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Preview Smoke Test
allObjections.detail: §4.4's preview smoke test only checks HTTP 2xx and presence of generic DOM elements like 'html' or 'body'. This fails to detect functional regressions in complex applications. For example, a broken checkout flow would pass this gate while being functionally unusable. The default selectors are too permissive to provide meaningful validation before PR creation.

allObjections.title: PAT Fallback Security Risk
allObjections.detail: §3.2's interim PAT fallback introduces long-lived credentials stored in Doppler, contradicting the memory-only principle in §8.1. The branch-scoping relies on operator-configured GitHub protections, which may be misconfigured. This creates an attack surface window before Phase B removal, especially since the fallback is triggered automatically when App installation lags.

allObjections.title: Delta Threshold Policy Conflict
allObjections.detail: §6.4's selfRenewalMinimumDelta and selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy interact poorly. A negative delta below the minimum threshold would trigger branch deletion without audit trail differentiation from positive-but-small deltas. This conflates two distinct failure modes in governance_record_entry, reducing diagnostic value for operators troubleshooting regressions.

allObjections.title: Re-assessment Cost Blindspot
allObjections.detail: Note 3 acknowledges doubled pipeline costs but provides no mitigation strategy. For products with frequent findings, the $0.60-$4.00 per-run cost could accumulate rapidly without budget controls. The spec lacks integration with Orchestra's cost dashboard or alerting mechanisms, risking unexpected operational expenses.

allObjections.title: Preview-before-PR deadlocks flow
allObjections.detail: §5.5 requires the Vercel preview to be live before the PR is opened, but §4.4 makes preview smoke a MUST gate and §5.5 says a failed preview can still yield a draft PR. Those rules conflict operationally: if preview build failure is what the operator most needs to inspect, the spec both forbids opening a PR and then immediately allows a draft PR, creating an ambiguous control path and likely branch clutter.

allObjections.title: Two credential paths expand attack surface
allObjections.detail: §3.2 keeps both GitHub App and PAT fallback in Phase A, with different storage, authorization, and branch-protection assumptions. That increases the number of ways a run can leak or mis-scope credentials, and the fallback is especially risky because it preserves a long-lived machine-user path precisely in the phase that is supposed to de-risk automation.

allObjections.title: Delta thresholds can hide regressions
allObjections.detail: §6.4 lets operators set `selfRenewalMinimumDelta` above zero and also optionally `DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE`, which means runs can be suppressed before a PR is ever opened. Combined with §6.5 making the audit trail the source of truth, this can systematically hide small but important regressions from human review even when the PR preview would have revealed them.

allObjections.title: Three-file cap misses semantic risk
allObjections.detail: §4.3 uses file count as the primary safety boundary, but a 2-file change can still be a major architectural mutation while a 6-file patch can be a trivial doc/string fix. The spec relies on diff-parse-time enforcement, yet the real risk surface is lines changed, coupling introduced, and dependency edges touched, not the raw number of files.

allObjections.title: Overly complex fix generation
allObjections.detail: §4.4 introduces multiple MUST gates (tests, typecheck, preview-smoke) that may be too strict or too lax, potentially leading to false positives or negatives in fix validation.

allObjections.title: Credential management risk
allObjections.detail: §3.2 retains a fine-grained PAT as an interim fallback, which adds attack surface and may be forgotten in Phase B, potentially leading to security vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: Lack of explicit regression handling
allObjections.detail: §2 and §7.5 highlight that Self-Renewal cannot guarantee no regressions until Phase D, relying on human review as the canonical regression gate, which may be error-prone.

allObjections.title: §3.2 App/PAT dual credential paths
allObjections.detail: The primary GitHub App + documented INTERIM PAT fallback in §3.2 creates two credential surfaces with separate Doppler paths and selection logic; the fallback emits governance_record_entry on every use but still requires branch-protection rules and machine-user setup that must be manually maintained until Phase B deletes it.

allObjections.title: §6.4 negative-delta + minimum-delta policies
allObjections.detail: ProductRegistry.selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy and selfRenewalMinimumDelta allow per-product tuning after the fact, yet the decision sequence in §6.4 still opens PRs under ALWAYS_OPEN even when delta_total ≤ 0; this can flood the operator inbox with regression banners while the audit trail is preserved only in governance_record_entry.

allObjections.title: Note 1 source-acquisition duplication
allObjections.detail: api/_lib/sourceAcquisition.js (tarball, read-only) and §3.5 (Contents + Git Data API, read-write) both read the same PRODUCT_<productId>_GITHUB_PAT credential; the spec only notes that Phase A should refactor them but provides no unified boundary or single-run credential lifetime guarantee.

strongest_rejection_argument.text: The proposal for the Self-Renewal feature is incomplete and lacks sufficient testing, evaluation, and validation. The feature's reliance on Claude for fix generation and the lack of human oversight could lead to unforeseen consequences and errors. Therefore, it is recommended to reject the proposal and require further development and testing before considering implementation. Specifically, the proposal should be revised to include more comprehensive testing, evaluation, and validation of the Self-Renewal feature, as well as more detailed information on how human oversight will be implemented and enforced.

objections.title: Preview-smoke gate has trivial bypass
objections.detail: §4.4 gate (c) accepts default selectors ['html', 'body'] which any broken app satisfies. A completely white-screened React app with a JS error still passes because the HTML skeleton renders, making this gate theatrical rather than functional.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The spec enables FlowAI to automatically push broken code to public GitHub repos and Vercel previews that are internet-accessible, creating a public attack surface for malicious actors to exploit half-fixed vulnerabilities before human review.
adversarial.precedent: Dependabot's early auto-PR system created similar review fatigue when it opened dozens of dependency update PRs without meaningful filtering, leading many teams to disable it entirely rather than wade through low-value automated changes.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This spec should be rejected because it fundamentally misaligns incentives: operators pay for expensive re-assessments ($0.65-$5 per run) while receiving PRs that may degrade their products (negative delta), creating a system where FlowAI profits from generating noise. The 3-file scope expansion without architectural understanding guarantees that fixes touching multiple files will be internally inconsistent, and the preview-smoke gate's default ['html','body'] configuration provides false confidence while allowing broken applications through.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: File-count framing misses the real risk — Phase A should cap by total diff hunk count or LOC changed (e.g. ≤ 50 LOC across all files), not file count.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: A 3-file change could modify thousands of lines while a 5-file change might touch only 10 lines total; the risk correlates with change magnitude, not file count.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Too strict — typecheck-skip-when-no-tsconfig and DOM-default ["html","body"] are loopholes; either MUST-universal or drop the gates entirely.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: The typecheck gate only applies to TypeScript projects and the preview-smoke gate's default selectors are meaningless, creating an inconsistent safety posture.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Drop the PAT fallback entirely from Phase A — App-only from day one; products without App installation cannot use Self-Renewal until they install. PAT fallback adds attack surface Phase B has to remove anyway.
G-Q3-v2.rationale: Maintaining two credential paths increases complexity and the PAT fallback contradicts the security controls in §8.1 by requiring long-lived token storage.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Wrong axis — policy should not be operator-configurable at all; tie to Authority posture (Supervised → ALWAYS_OPEN, Autonomous → DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) per CA-12 v3 §A.2.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Making this operator-configurable allows them to hide FlowAI's failures; the policy should be deterministic based on the authority model to maintain transparency.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Threshold should be per-layer not just delta_total — operators may care about L1 Functionality regressions even when delta_total is positive; expose as per-Five-Layer map.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: A positive total delta could hide critical L1 functionality regressions; operators need granular control to prevent user-facing breakage.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 5 edits is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The preview-smoke gate (Q2 condition) is ineffective with default selectors, and the cost implications of re-assessment weren't addressed despite being a fundamental operational concern.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The spec's core flaw is treating symptoms (findings) without understanding system architecture, guaranteeing that multi-file fixes will be internally inconsistent.

G-Q6-v2.rationale: Setting a default of +1 ensures that only meaningful improvements are surfaced, reducing noise and focusing reviewer attention on significant changes.

G-Q2-v2.rationale: The three MUST gates provide a comprehensive set of checks to ensure the quality of the fixes.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: App-primary + INTERIM PAT-fallback is correct — App is long-term right answer; fallback is pragmatic migration affordance Phase B retires (App provisioned + ≥3 of 5 products installed).
G-Q3-v2.rationale: The GitHub App provides a more secure and scalable solution, while the PAT fallback allows for a smooth transition.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Per-product enum (ALWAYS_OPEN | DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) is correct — different products have different reviewer-bandwidth profiles; operator choice with ALWAYS_OPEN default is the right balance.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Allowing operators to choose the negative-delta policy provides flexibility and accommodates different product needs.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Per-product integer with default 0 is correct — operator decides 'what counts as worth my review time'; default of 0 preserves surface-everything posture for operators who don't tune.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: The default of 0 allows operators to review all changes, while still providing the option to set a higher threshold if desired.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Reject — 5 edits expose a deeper architectural problem with Option C that surgical revisions cannot fix; spec needs ground-up rework or replacement (specify architectural concern).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The proposal introduces significant changes without sufficient testing and validation, and relies heavily on human review, making it unsuitable for promotion at this time.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal requires further refinement and testing before it can be considered for promotion.

objections.title: Credential Fallback Complexity
objections.detail: §3.2 introduces significant complexity with the GitHub App primary and PAT fallback.  Managing two credential paths increases the attack surface and operational overhead, especially during the transition period. The logic for selecting and validating the correct credential adds potential for errors and vulnerabilities.

objections.title: Limited Regression Detection
objections.detail: §2 acknowledges the inability to guarantee no regressions, relying heavily on human review.  While §7.5 mentions Phase D will address this, the current reliance on human review is a significant risk, especially as the number of automated fixes increases. The test suite may not cover all edge cases, and visual regressions can easily be missed.

objections.title: Re-assessment Cost
objections.detail: §6.2 and Note 3 highlight the cost of re-running the full 8-step pipeline for re-assessment.  This doubles the assessment cost and significantly increases the overall cost of the Self-Renewal cycle.  The cost may become prohibitive, especially for products with frequent renewal runs.

objections.title: Preview Smoke Test Weakness
objections.detail: §4.4 (c) defines the preview smoke test as checking for HTTP 2xx and at least one key DOM element. The default DOM element check of `['html', 'body']` is effectively useless.  Even with stricter selectors, this provides minimal assurance that the preview is actually functional or visually correct.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the Self-Renewal process introduces regressions that are not caught by the limited testing and human review, it could lead to broken production deployments and a degradation of the overall system. This would be worse than the current state where issues are identified but not automatically fixed.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: While the proposal aims to automate the fix-and-preview cycle, the reliance on human review for regression detection and the complexity of the credential fallback mechanism introduce significant risks. The cost of re-assessment and the weakness of the preview smoke test further undermine the value proposition. Deferring the proposal would allow for a more thorough evaluation of these risks and a refinement of the testing and credential management strategies.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: File-count framing misses the real risk — Phase A should cap by total diff hunk count or LOC changed (e.g. ≤ 50 LOC across all files), not file count.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: Limiting by file count is arbitrary. A small change across many files is less risky than a large change in a single file. LOC or hunk count provides a better measure of complexity.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Too lax — Phase A should also MUST-gate accessibility (axe-core) and visual regression (screenshot diff against pre-renewal baseline) before any PR opens.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: Accessibility and visual regressions are critical aspects of quality. Failing to include these in the MUST gates leaves a significant gap in the automated testing process.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Drop the PAT fallback entirely from Phase A — App-only from day one; products without App installation cannot use Self-Renewal until they install. PAT fallback adds attack surface Phase B has to remove anyway.
G-Q3-v2.rationale: The PAT fallback introduces unnecessary complexity and security risks. Enforcing App-only from day one simplifies the credential management and reduces the attack surface.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Over-engineered — Phase A should hard-code ALWAYS_OPEN (transparency-first) until usage data justifies a per-product knob; one configurable flag per minor design choice is config-creep.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Configurability should be added only when there is a clear need. Starting with ALWAYS_OPEN simplifies the initial implementation and allows for data-driven decisions about future configurability.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Threshold should be per-layer not just delta_total — operators may care about L1 Functionality regressions even when delta_total is positive; expose as per-Five-Layer map.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: A single total delta can mask regressions in specific layers. Providing per-layer thresholds allows operators to focus on the areas that are most important to them.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Promote-with-Reservations — 5 conditions addressed but Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (non-blocking; specify in rationale).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The proposal addresses the previous conditions, but the issues with regression detection, credential complexity, re-assessment cost, and preview smoke test weakness warrant careful tracking during the engineering dispatch.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is a step in the right direction, but the risks and limitations need to be carefully considered during implementation. Addressing the identified weaknesses will be crucial for the success of Self-Renewal.

objections.title: Insufficient Preview Smoke Test
objections.detail: §4.4's preview smoke test only checks HTTP 2xx and presence of generic DOM elements like 'html' or 'body'. This fails to detect functional regressions in complex applications. For example, a broken checkout flow would pass this gate while being functionally unusable. The default selectors are too permissive to provide meaningful validation before PR creation.

objections.title: PAT Fallback Security Risk
objections.detail: §3.2's interim PAT fallback introduces long-lived credentials stored in Doppler, contradicting the memory-only principle in §8.1. The branch-scoping relies on operator-configured GitHub protections, which may be misconfigured. This creates an attack surface window before Phase B removal, especially since the fallback is triggered automatically when App installation lags.

objections.title: Delta Threshold Policy Conflict
objections.detail: §6.4's selfRenewalMinimumDelta and selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy interact poorly. A negative delta below the minimum threshold would trigger branch deletion without audit trail differentiation from positive-but-small deltas. This conflates two distinct failure modes in governance_record_entry, reducing diagnostic value for operators troubleshooting regressions.

objections.title: Re-assessment Cost Blindspot
objections.detail: Note 3 acknowledges doubled pipeline costs but provides no mitigation strategy. For products with frequent findings, the $0.60-$4.00 per-run cost could accumulate rapidly without budget controls. The spec lacks integration with Orchestra's cost dashboard or alerting mechanisms, risking unexpected operational expenses.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the preview smoke test passes but introduces subtle business logic flaws (e.g., miscalculated pricing), operators might merge PRs based on positive delta scores. This could deploy broken functionality to production faster than manual review, whereas the status quo's slower human process would likely catch such issues during code examination.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub Actions token leakage incidents (2022-2023) where long-lived credentials stored in Doppler equivalents were exfiltrated via environment variable mishandling, leading to repository compromises. Similar risks exist with PAT fallback despite scrubCredentials() protections.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal introduces substantial new attack surfaces (GitHub write access, PAT storage) and cost liabilities (doubled pipeline runs) without commensurate safety mechanisms. The discard gates remain easily gameable—LLMs could satisfy DOM checks while breaking key flows—and the per-product configuration complexity risks misconfiguration. Given the skeleton state of Agent #3, deferring until Phase A proves its security invariants in staging would be prudent.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: File-count framing misses the real risk — Phase A should cap by total diff hunk count or LOC changed (e.g. ≤ 50 LOC across all files), not file count.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: A 3-file change could still introduce massive refactors (e.g., 500+ LOC). LOC/hunk limits directly constrain change magnitude, aligning better with human review capacity.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Too lax — Phase A should also MUST-gate accessibility (axe-core) and visual regression (screenshot diff against pre-renewal baseline) before any PR opens.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: Current gates miss UI-layer regressions critical for operator trust. Axe-core is lightweight; screenshot diffs could sample key pages to catch rendering breaks.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Drop the PAT fallback entirely from Phase A — App-only from day one; products without App installation cannot use Self-Renewal until they install. PAT fallback adds attack surface Phase B has to remove anyway.
G-Q3-v2.rationale: The interim PAT creates immediate security debt. Installation friction is a feature forcing explicit operator consent, not a bug.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Per-product enum (ALWAYS_OPEN | DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) is correct — different products have different reviewer-bandwidth profiles; operator choice with ALWAYS_OPEN default is the right balance.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Operators managing critical systems may need to see regressions immediately, while others may filter noise. The enum preserves flexibility without overcomplication.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Per-product integer with default 0 is correct — operator decides 'what counts as worth my review time'; default of 0 preserves surface-everything posture for operators who don't tune.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: MinimumDelta complements NegativeDeltaPolicy by filtering trivial wins. Per-layer thresholds would overcomplicate Phase A.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 5 edits is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: Q3's PAT fallback introduces security flaws, and Q2's smoke test remains inadequate. These require resolution before promotion.

perReviewer.overallNotes: While v2 addresses surface concerns, foundational security and validation gaps remain. PAT fallback must be eliminated, and preview validation strengthened to prevent functional regressions.

objections.title: Preview-before-PR deadlocks flow
objections.detail: §5.5 requires the Vercel preview to be live before the PR is opened, but §4.4 makes preview smoke a MUST gate and §5.5 says a failed preview can still yield a draft PR. Those rules conflict operationally: if preview build failure is what the operator most needs to inspect, the spec both forbids opening a PR and then immediately allows a draft PR, creating an ambiguous control path and likely branch clutter.

objections.title: Two credential paths expand attack surface
objections.detail: §3.2 keeps both GitHub App and PAT fallback in Phase A, with different storage, authorization, and branch-protection assumptions. That increases the number of ways a run can leak or mis-scope credentials, and the fallback is especially risky because it preserves a long-lived machine-user path precisely in the phase that is supposed to de-risk automation.

objections.title: Delta thresholds can hide regressions
objections.detail: §6.4 lets operators set `selfRenewalMinimumDelta` above zero and also optionally `DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE`, which means runs can be suppressed before a PR is ever opened. Combined with §6.5 making the audit trail the source of truth, this can systematically hide small but important regressions from human review even when the PR preview would have revealed them.

objections.title: Three-file cap misses semantic risk
objections.detail: §4.3 uses file count as the primary safety boundary, but a 2-file change can still be a major architectural mutation while a 6-file patch can be a trivial doc/string fix. The spec relies on diff-parse-time enforcement, yet the real risk surface is lines changed, coupling introduced, and dependency edges touched, not the raw number of files.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If Self-Renewal starts auto-fixing, opening previews, and then suppresses PR creation whenever the preview build or delta threshold fails, operators may lose the visible paper trail they currently get from a pure analysis-only system. In that scenario the system produces hidden branch churn and partial audit records without delivering a reviewable artifact, which is worse than the current analyzer-only status quo.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub Actions and similar CI/CD bots have repeatedly created branch-management and credential-scoping incidents when mixing bot tokens, branch protection exceptions, and auto-generated PRs; a well-known class of failures is automation creating or updating PRs in ways maintainers did not expect, especially when fallback credentials exist.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring this spec is that it tries to land too many high-risk capabilities at once: source acquisition, code mutation, preview deployment, re-assessment, scoring, and policy-driven PR suppression. Each layer has distinct failure modes, and the spec still depends on a human to catch regressions, which means the complexity cost may exceed the marginal benefit over the current analyzer-only flow. Deferring until the authority model, credential model, and suppression rules are simpler would likely reduce operational risk and make failures easier to diagnose.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: 3-file cap is too permissive — Phase A should keep single-file scope until ≥30 days in production; raise to 3 only in Phase B.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: The spec’s own safety story rests on Phase A being narrowly bounded, but the 3-file allowance broadens blast radius before there is live evidence. Single-file scope is easier to reason about and aligns better with the draft’s claim that Phase B should absorb broader refactors.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Three MUST gates (test + typecheck + preview-smoke) is correct — each catches a distinct failure class (logic / type / runtime-SSR regression); none redundant.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: These gates are complementary rather than duplicative, and the preview-smoke check adds a real-world rendering signal that tests alone cannot provide. The spec also appropriately skips typecheck when no tsconfig exists, avoiding a universal false blocker for non-TS repos.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: App-primary + INTERIM PAT-fallback is correct — App is long-term right answer; fallback is pragmatic migration affordance Phase B retires (App provisioned + ≥3 of 5 products installed).
G-Q3-v2.rationale: This is the least disruptive migration path while still making the secure credential model the long-term default. The fallback is ugly, but the spec includes a concrete retirement trigger rather than leaving PAT use open-ended.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Per-product enum (ALWAYS_OPEN | DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) is correct — different products have different reviewer-bandwidth profiles; operator choice with ALWAYS_OPEN default is the right balance.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: This policy is genuinely a product-level preference, not a universal invariant, so making it configurable is defensible. The default preserves transparency while allowing bandwidth-constrained teams to suppress low-value regression PRs.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Per-product integer with default 0 is correct — operator decides "what counts as worth my review time"; default of 0 preserves surface-everything posture for operators who don't tune.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: A default of zero avoids silently hiding borderline improvements and keeps the system maximally observable unless the operator opts out. Thresholding by total delta is crude, but acceptable as a first-order control as long as the audit trail remains intact.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 5 edits is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The preview-before-PR / preview-failure draft-PR behavior is not fully coherent, and the combined policy knobs for negative delta and minimum delta can suppress important review artifacts. The architecture is promising, but these inconsistencies mean it is not yet ready for promotion as written.

perReviewer.overallNotes: My vote is not a rejection of the direction, but of the current draft’s operational coherence. The proposal needs another pass to simplify the failure paths and make the preview/PR ordering unambiguous.

objections.title: Overly complex fix generation
objections.detail: §4.4 introduces multiple MUST gates (tests, typecheck, preview-smoke) that may be too strict or too lax, potentially leading to false positives or negatives in fix validation.

objections.title: Credential management risk
objections.detail: §3.2 retains a fine-grained PAT as an interim fallback, which adds attack surface and may be forgotten in Phase B, potentially leading to security vulnerabilities.

objections.title: Lack of explicit regression handling
objections.detail: §2 and §7.5 highlight that Self-Renewal cannot guarantee no regressions until Phase D, relying on human review as the canonical regression gate, which may be error-prone.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the fix generation and validation gates are too strict, it may lead to a significant number of false negatives, making the system worse than the status quo by missing potential fixes.
adversarial.precedent: Similar complex AI-driven code generation systems have faced challenges with false positives/negatives and security vulnerabilities, such as GitHub Copilot's early versions.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal's reliance on multiple complex gates and AI-driven fix generation without a clear mechanism for handling regressions or ensuring the quality of generated fixes across different products and environments could lead to inconsistent outcomes and potential security risks.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: 3-file cap with diff-parse-time enforcement is correct — covers common multi-file patterns (component + test + parent route) while preventing LLM scope sprawl; parse-time discard is a structural guarantee.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: The 3-file cap seems reasonable for Phase A as it balances the need for multi-file fixes with the risk of scope sprawl.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Three MUST gates (test + typecheck + preview-smoke) is correct — each catches a distinct failure class (logic / type / runtime-SSR regression); none redundant.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: The three gates cover different aspects of potential regressions, making them complementary and necessary for robust validation.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: App-primary + INTERIM PAT-fallback is correct — App is long-term right answer; fallback is pragmatic migration affordance Phase B retires (App provisioned + ≥3 of 5 products installed).
G-Q3-v2.rationale: Using the GitHub App as primary with a PAT fallback for migration seems like a reasonable approach, given the need for a smooth transition.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Per-product enum (ALWAYS_OPEN | DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) is correct — different products have different reviewer-bandwidth profiles; operator choice with ALWAYS_OPEN default is the right balance.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Allowing operators to choose based on their product's needs is sensible, and the default setting ensures transparency.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Per-product integer with default 0 is correct — operator decides "what counts as worth my review time"; default of 0 preserves surface-everything posture for operators who don't tune.
G-Q6-v2.rationale: This approach gives operators flexibility while maintaining a default that surfaces all results.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Promote-with-Reservations — 5 conditions addressed but Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (non-blocking; specify in rationale).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: While the 5 conditions are addressed, there are still concerns regarding the complexity of the gates and the reliance on human review for regression handling that should be tracked.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is generally well-structured but has areas that require careful consideration and monitoring, particularly around the complexity of fix validation and regression handling.

objections.title: §3.2 App/PAT dual credential paths
objections.detail: The primary GitHub App + documented INTERIM PAT fallback in §3.2 creates two credential surfaces with separate Doppler paths and selection logic; the fallback emits governance_record_entry on every use but still requires branch-protection rules and machine-user setup that must be manually maintained until Phase B deletes it.

objections.title: §6.4 negative-delta + minimum-delta policies
objections.detail: ProductRegistry.selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy and selfRenewalMinimumDelta allow per-product tuning after the fact, yet the decision sequence in §6.4 still opens PRs under ALWAYS_OPEN even when delta_total ≤ 0; this can flood the operator inbox with regression banners while the audit trail is preserved only in governance_record_entry.

objections.title: Note 1 source-acquisition duplication
objections.detail: api/_lib/sourceAcquisition.js (tarball, read-only) and §3.5 (Contents + Git Data API, read-write) both read the same PRODUCT_<productId>_GITHUB_PAT credential; the spec only notes that Phase A should refactor them but provides no unified boundary or single-run credential lifetime guarantee.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the PAT fallback is used on even one product and the branch-protection rules are misconfigured, a compromised Self-Renewal run can push to flowai/* branches that later get merged by a distracted reviewer, introducing untested code into production faster than the prior manual-fix workflow.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub's 2023 PAT rotation incident showed that long-lived fine-grained tokens scoped to specific branches still leaked via logs and CI artifacts when dual credential paths existed without a single enforced boundary.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal layers five new per-product registry fields, two credential paths, three MUST gates, and a full re-assessment pipeline on top of an already complex Self-Governance and Clearance system; this increases attack surface and operational surface area before any production data shows that the simpler single-file analyzer in the current Agent #3 skeleton is insufficient.

G-Q1-v2.pick_text: 3-file cap is too permissive — Phase A should keep single-file scope until ≥30 days in production; raise to 3 only in Phase B.
G-Q1-v2.rationale: The parse-time enforcement is welcome but the jump from 1 to 3 files still risks scope sprawl before real usage data exists.

G-Q2-v2.pick_text: Too lax — Phase A should also MUST-gate accessibility (axe-core) and visual regression (screenshot diff against pre-renewal baseline) before any PR opens.
G-Q2-v2.rationale: Adding typecheck and preview-smoke is positive but still omits common regression classes that human reviewers will otherwise have to catch manually.

G-Q3-v2.pick_text: Drop the PAT fallback entirely from Phase A — App-only from day one; products without App installation cannot use Self-Renewal until they install. PAT fallback adds attack surface Phase B has to remove anyway.
G-Q3-v2.rationale: The interim path duplicates credential handling and creates exactly the dual-surface risk highlighted in the adversarial pass.

G-Q4-v2.pick_text: Wrong axis — policy should not be operator-configurable at all; tie to Authority posture (Supervised → ALWAYS_OPEN, Autonomous → DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) per CA-12 v3 §A.2.
G-Q4-v2.rationale: Per-product knobs increase configuration debt without addressing the core supervised-authority contract already defined elsewhere.

G-Q6-v2.pick_text: Threshold mechanism is redundant with G-Q4 DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE — drop per-product integer; collapse into single 3-state enum (ALL | IMPROVEMENTS_ONLY | SUBSTANTIAL_ONLY).
G-Q6-v2.rationale: Two separate numeric and enum controls on the same delta value create overlapping and potentially conflicting policy surfaces.

G-Q7-v2.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 5 edits is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7-v2.rationale: The credential-duplication and policy-overlap issues introduced by the v2 edits must be resolved before any engineering dispatch.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The spec correctly narrows scope to supervised PR+preview but still underestimates the cumulative complexity added to the existing Self-Governance and Clearance layers.
